text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: spike in 5xx + DNS NXDOMAINs from us-east-2c beginning ~1876543200. Impacting inbound traffic to services behind private subnets. Paging oncall (maria).

maria: ACKing, looking. seeing NXDOMAIN for internal service names from instances in az-2c only. Ping to nat gw times out from those subnets.

raj: did we push any NACL/route changes in that AZ in the last deploy window?

maria: checking audit logs... running: `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0a123bcd` to confirm.

maria: logs show an automated infra job modified a NACL rule at 12:03 UTC (allow->deny ephemeral ports). seems targeted to the env patch job.

lee: oh no, that job had a bug that made ephemeral port range deny instead of restrict. that would break NAT source ports and break DNS over UDP/TCP for outbound. rolling back now.

netops-bot: rollback initiated by lee using runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/nat-nacl-rollback. Estimated completion 4 minutes.

maria: temporary mitigation - we're adding a host-route for 8.8.8.8 via alternate nat in az-2b to see if DNS queries recover. command: 
```
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0f12ab34 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-0cdef123
```

sophie: customer-success: which customers are seeing errors? we have two paying customers on the affected AZ with active sessions (acme-inc, betaapp). I warned support and opened CS tickets.

maria: DNS is improving after the route addition. NXDOMAIN rate down from 18% -> 2% in 3 mins. still some spikes. reverting the bad NACL change now. command: 
```
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0a1b2c3d --rule-number 100 --protocol "-1" --rule-action allow --egress
```

raj: confirmed NACL entry replaced. doing `curl -v http://internal-service.local/health` from a bastion in az-2c -> 200 OK.

lee: rolling some extra checks to ensure we didn't accidentally shadow-route traffic: `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0a123bcd` and checking for stale route propagations.

maria: oncall handoff incoming. I'm going to capture mitigation steps and impact, then hand to raj for post-incident follow-up.

maria: Handoff notes for next oncall (raj): 
- What happened: automated infra patch job incorrectly updated NACL in az-2c, blocking ephemeral/outbound ports -> NAT health degraded -> DNS NXDOMAIN and 5xx on service frontends.
- Mitigation performed: temporary route to alternate NAT in az-2b, then rolled back NACL via replace-network-acl-entry. Verified service health and DNS.
- Commands run: see earlier commands. CloudTrail event id: evt-04c3f2.
- Customer impact: short blip affecting TCP/UDP outbound from private subnets in az-2c; ACME and BetaApp saw transient errors (~2-6 minutes). No data loss.
- Next steps: runbook link + recommend disabling the infra job or patching its rule template to use allow with narrower ranges; run canary on staging for NACL changes.

raj: taking over. I'll open a follow-up ticket with infra team to patch job and require manual approval for NACL diffs. tagging @netops for deeper review.

netops-bot: Noted. Creating internal ticket NETOPS-947 for NACL automation review. Assigned to lee.

lee: I'll audit recent infra job changes and add a guard to reject deny-wide ephemeral-range diffs. Also will create an automated test to simulate NAT traffic after NACL changes.

maria: pinging support: please update customers ACME and BetaApp that root cause was misapplied NACL, mitigation succeeded, and we're taking steps to prevent recurrence. Suggested CS note: "We experienced a brief network configuration issue in one AZ that impacted outbound NAT and DNS for a subset of our infrastructure. We've reverted the change and implemented a mitigation; services are back to normal. No customer data was affected."

customer-success: acknowledged, sending messages now.

raj: post-incident checklist:
- severity: S3 (partial outage affecting subset of customers for 2-6 mins)
- timeline: 12:03 change -> 12:06 alerts -> 12:07 temp route -> 12:10 NACL revert -> 12:12 verified recovery -> 12:15 notify customers
- impact: internal DNS and outbound from az-2c private subnets; frontend 5xx spike observed by synthetic monitors and customer traffic.

maria: adding retrospective owners: lee (automation fix), raj (follow-up ticket + postmortem writeup), sopie (customer communications). leaving channel.

maria: :white_check_mark: resolved? marking incident-bot with resolved tag and short summary.

incident-bot: Incident resolved by maria. Summary: NACL automation change in az-2c caused NAT health and DNS failures; temporary routing and NACL rollback restored service. Follow-ups: NETOPS-947, PM-io to update runbook.

raj: filing final postmortem now; will include the packet captures and CloudTrail sequence in the doc.

lee: quick note for SRE: please consider enabling an egress-probe synthetic from each AZ to catch NAT port exhaustion / NACL changes in future. small canary every minute should catch this earlier.

maria: agreed. thanks everyone. :heart:
